Just an ordinary visit, or a possible courtship?
First Lady Liza Araneta made a surprise visit to the Batasang Pambansa on Tuesday, November 24, and of course, no less than Speaker Bojie Dy welcomed and accompanied her.

The joint public appearance comes amid rumors that Dy is being strongly considered to become President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s number two, should Vice President Sara Duterte be found guilty by the impeachment court and removed from office.

Malacañang or the House are unlikely to confirm anything more than what the visit was supposed to be on paper: the First Lady attending an arts workshop and storytelling session for children at the House.
Marcos, accompanied by Dy and other House leaders, checked the exhibits in celebration of National Children’s Month.
The Palace isn’t stupid and should be vetting by now all the possible replacements of Vice President Duterte, whose impeachment case is now in the final stages at the Senate.
Should at least 14 senators vote to convict her over her supposed unexplained wealth, the vice presidency will be a vacant position that the President needs to fill.
The Constitution allows the President to nominate a replacement from among members of the Senate and the House.
Aside from Dy, other lawmakers who are supposedly being considered for the job include Escudero, Win Gatchalian, Tito Sotto, and Lito Lapid.

As we previously reported, Dy is an attractive pick for the president. He does not have ambitions for higher office in 2028, sometimes plays second fiddle to the President’s son, Majority Leader Sandro Marcos, in the House, and is still respected by his colleagues despite the perceived ceremonial nature of his power.

blocks.caption: Bojie Dy, the unexciting Speaker whom Marcos can count on

blocks.text: While Sandro is a lawmaker himself, the President cannot pick his son because he is only 32 years old, below the constitutional age requirement of 40.
The First Lady is known to have the President’s ear, and insiders say she is actively involved in managing the many affairs of the Palace.
It wouldn’t be farfetched to imagine how the vice presidency problem could also be on her plate, but we can only speculate. – Rappler.com
